purpose: Every French action name renamed to English. Continuous with docs/action-parameter-renames.json (ticket 22): together they are the input to the later migration that rewrites {{action param="..."}} in stored page bodies. That migration is deliberately NOT part of either ticket -- decided 2026-07-31, 'documented breaking changes now, migration magic later'. Apply this file's renames BEFORE that one's: action-parameter-renames.json is keyed by the action name as it was spelled in ticket 22, which is exactly how an unmigrated body still spells it.

handlerPolicy.decision: No handler is renamed, so no handler URL changes and no redirecting alias is needed.
handlerPolicy.why: The ticket flagged handler names as its one place where a compatibility mechanism might be worth its cost, because /MyPage/revisions and friends are bookmarked and linked from outside. On inspection every one of the 24 handler names is already English -- acls, addcomment, claim, deletepage, duplicate, edit, editiframe, emailactivation, filemanager, html, iframe, listpages, mail, qrcodetroc, raw, render, revisions, rss, sendmail, share, show, tagrss, update, xml. There was nothing to decide.
handlerPolicy.consequence: Inbound links keep working. The break is confined to page bodies, which a migration can reach.

conventions.case: All-lowercase with no separators, matching how an action is typed in a page body.
conventions.classes: 11 classes were renamed alongside so that a class and its performableName() agree again -- leaving EntryListAction::performableName() returning 'bazarliste' would be exactly the half-rename ticket 22 got bitten by.
conventions.values: Action PARAMETER names are ticket 22's; parameter VALUES and template filenames are user data and unchanged. {{searchform template="moteurrecherche_button.twig"}} is correct and deliberate: the action moved, the template filename did not.

renames.note: the action's own vocabulary moved with it: the `demand` template variable and the ContactApiController `type` it posts back are now subscribe/unsubscribe. The `form-abonnement` CSS class is a class name and stays
admin* rather than manage*, matching the admintag / admincontent / adminreactions / adminbackups actions already in core
the {{include}} parameter of the same name became `doubleclick` in ticket 22; this is the action. The `allow_doubleclic` config key and the `doubleclickedit` user column are stored data and unchanged
renders the search FORM. Ticket 18 plans a separate {{search}} action that performs the search; the two must stay distinguishable

unchanged.name: bazar
unchanged.why: the BazaR admin console, not an entry -- there is no entry* name that describes it. Decided 2026-08-01: `bazar` is the product's own word for this screen, like `wiki`, and `{{bazar}}` is the single most-used action in YesWiki, so it is the one place where not breaking content is worth an inconsistency

unchanged.name: bazarcard, bazarcalendar, bazaragenda, bazarannuaire, bazartimeline, bazarcarousel, bazarlistephotobox, bazarlisteliens, bazarblog, bazargogocarto, bazartableau, bazarmapandtable
unchanged.why: actions-builder PRESET ids in docs/actions/entrylist.yaml, not actions. Every one of them emits {{entrylist template="..."}}; they never appear in a page body. They carry YAML anchors and AB_* translation keys, so renaming them is churn with real breakage risk and no user-visible payoff

unchanged.why: asset and template FILENAMES -- addressable from page bodies, so user data, same rule ticket 21 applied

alsoFixed: LinkTracker::preventNotTrackingActions() matched `gerertheme` (singular, no such action), so theme-management action calls were never actually excluded from link tracking. Corrected to `adminthemes` while renaming.

themes/yeswiki/squelettes/1col.twig still passed ticket 22's old parameter spellings `doubleclic="1"` and `actif="1"` to {{include}}. Ticket 22's sweep covered src/ and templates/ but not themes/; caught and fixed here.

migration.why: per-action ACLs live in wakka.config.php under `permissions.action.<name>`, so a rename orphans the entry and the action silently falls back to `*` (everybody). That is a permissions regression that opens up rather than locks down, so unlike the page-body rewrite it is not deferred.
